target_customer: FMCG distributors in Nigeria buying stock, and the manufacturers that sell to them and want payment or financing
problem: Distributors in Africa cannot easily get credit to buy inventory from manufacturers, while manufacturers struggle to collect payments and finance distributor purchases.
business_model: Inventory financing and payments for distributors through the Obtainly app (earlier a B2B marketplace); fee structure not public
product_category: B2B fintech: supply chain payments and inventory credit

founders.name: Sefa Ikyaator
founders.background_notes: YC profile calls him a Retail Distribution Expert. The YC company text says the team has 25+ combined years in supply chain and ecommerce at Procter and Gamble, PepsiCo, Gap and Jumia, without assigning employers to individuals.

founders.name: Stephen Igwue
founders.background_notes: His YC profile says he was previously founding CTO at Suplias (S21); individual employers and education not found.

competitors.name: TradeDepot
competitors.what: Nigerian B2B platform connecting FMCG manufacturers and distributors to informal retailers, expanding into financial services and credit
competitors.funding_then: About 10 million dollars raised as of July 2020 per TechCabal headline

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app plus payments and credit scoring in Nigeria is standard engineering; the hard parts were underwriting and compliance rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Manufacturer relationships and credit data could accumulate, but better-funded rivals such as TradeDepot were already adding credit.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals with far more funding built credit offerings for retailers; no source shows any of them acquiring or copying Suplias specifically.

market_need_then: A May 2021 Techpoint style piece reported that Nigerian retailers could access only about 30 percent of their credit needs, and a 2021 article cited about 5 percent bad debt and 15 percent overdue credit among distributors.

branding.domain_note: Uses suplias.com, the exact .com; history not found.

identity.visual_style: Illustrations of African commerce including cowrie shells, a farming hoe and a cargo tricycle (company site)
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-led: Building the Engine of Commerce in Africa

brand_strength.rationale: Only YC and press coverage of the batch were found; the consumer-facing brand became Obtainly, and the company now uses a sub-brand structure with Obtainly and 360credit.

pivots.from: B2B marketplace letting small retailers buy inventory from manufacturers
pivots.to: Inventory financing and payments for FMCG distributors via Obtainly
pivots.why: Reported by Yespress as driven by retailer feedback; date not stated

outcome_analysis: Suplias entered YC Summer 2021 as a Nigerian B2B marketplace for retailer inventory and moved toward credit and payments for FMCG distributors under the Obtainly app. It is still listed as Active with a team of 9 and a site showing 2019 to 2026. Disclosed funding is small and inconsistent across aggregators, and no exit, failure or later priced round was found. It faced much better funded Nigerian rivals already moving into credit.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding: StartupList says 125K seed led by YC in July 2021, iamsterdam says 130K, Liners and Yespress say about 260K total. The Disrupt Africa and Business Insider Africa 2021 articles linked from the YC page were not opened. None of these amounts is recorded as a round because I could only see them in aggregators or snippets. Investors list comes from the company site. Atacama Ventures appeared in a snippet only. The retailer credit statistics came from search snippets of a 2021 article. No shutdown or acquisition found. No dated competitor search beyond TradeDepot was sourced with a pre-batch link.
